## Purpose

Hosts `RunConnectionProvider`, **the single app-level owner of the SSE run connection(s)** —
mounted above the router so live-run streams survive route changes (navigating to the wizard,
handoff, or fullscreen no longer tears down the transport).

Depends on `@/hooks/useRunStream` and `@/lib` (API client, env, SSE frame parsing); consumed by
the app shell, layout components, and `@/hooks` itself (`useWorkflow` reads
`useRunConnection()` to send commands).

## Shape

- [RunConnectionProvider.tsx](../../frontend/src/providers/RunConnectionProvider.tsx) — a React context provider. On mount/reconnect it does a
  server-derived reattach: queries `GET /api/runs` filtered to non-terminal runs and attaches
  one `useRunStream` per live run. **It never trusts `sessionStorage` alone to decide what's
  live** — a persisted per-run cursor is only a `Last-Event-ID` resume hint.

  `AUTO_STREAM_STATUSES` is the actively-emitting subset of non-terminal statuses (`running`,
  `planning`, `analyzing`, `generating`, `revising`), deliberately excluding the parked statuses
  `clarifying`/`waiting_for_user`, which would otherwise burn a socket in the browser's
  ~6-connections-per-origin pool for zero live updates. The currently-viewed/launched run stays
  streamed even while parked via a sticky `focusedRunId`.

  Exposes `phase` (aggregate connection state), `liveRunIds`, `reattach()`, and an imperative
  `attachRun()` for launch-to-attach without waiting on the next poll. Also owns the
  streamed-POST up-channel (`sendCommand`), reusing `@/lib/sseFrame`'s `parseSseBlock` so up-
  and down-channel parse through the same code path.
- [RunConnectionProvider.test.tsx](../../frontend/src/providers/RunConnectionProvider.test.tsx) — the co-located vitest suite.

## Why this shape

Prior to this provider the SSE connection lived inside dashboard/page.tsx, so any navigation
away from the dashboard killed the transport mid-run. **Promoting ownership to a provider above
the router is the direct fix.**

The server-derived (never client-trusted) reattach exists because `sessionStorage` alone could
drift from what's actually still running server-side after a crash/refresh; re-querying
`GET /api/runs` is the source of truth, with the persisted cursor purely as an optimization (a
full replay is still correct, just slower, thanks to downstream `event_id` dedup in
`@/lib/wsReplayState`).

Excluding parked statuses from auto-streaming is a direct fix for a real socket-exhaustion bug
(BUG-013): every `fetch`-based SSE stream holds one of the browser's limited per-origin
connections, so **precision about which runs actually need a live stream is load-bearing, not an
optimization.**
